text: Guides

title: Why should I deposit data in the Faculty Research Data Collection?
text:
You should deposit data in the Faculty Research Data Collection for any ofthe following reasons:

To comply with funder or publisher data sharing requirements
Ensure reliable, managed access to data
Increase scholarly impact through discoverability
Collaborate with research teams
Select a CC0 or CC BY license

title: I have data that updates regularly, can I deposit it with the Faculty Research Data Collection?
text: The Faculty Research Data Collection is not designed to support continuously updated data, as all datasets must go through a manual curation and review process. Please reach out to librarydataservices@berkeley.edu if you would like to discuss depositing snapshots of dynamic data.

title: I want to publish my data in a different repository. What are my options?
text: The UC Berkeley Library provides memberships to a variety of repositories, including Dryad and ICPSR. Please contact librarydataservices@berkeley.edu for guidance.

title: What data protection levels are safe to deposit with the Faculty Research Data Collection?
text:
Data up to protection level 2 may be deposited with the Faculty Research Data Collection.
For guidance on data classification, review the Information Security Office’s How to Classify Research Data resource or contact the Research Data Management Program.

title: About
text:
UC Berkeley (UCB) Library Dataverse is a repository where users can find data relevant to the UC Berkeley Community and beyond, including datasets licensed for use in research, teaching, and learning, as well as research data generated by UC Berkeley faculty.
UC Berkeley Library Dataverse is managed and maintained by the Library’s Data + Digital Scholarship Services and Library IT. It is deployed using The Dataverse Project, an open-source repository software, and is distinct from Harvard Dataverse and other Dataverse installations around the world.
Datasets in UC Berkeley Library Dataverse can be found across three collections:
While some datasets in Dataverse are restricted, metadata and terms of use are viewable by anyone.

title: About
text:
Dataverse Collections

Licensed Data
The UC Berkeley Library licenses and acquires datasets for use by UC Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Lab students, faculty, and staff. If you cannot find the data you are looking for, please contact your subject librarian to identify a suitable alternative or suggest a purchase.
Please login to the repository using a Calnet ID and passphrase to view and download licensed data files. Note that accessing some data files requires agreeing to the terms of use and registering with a guestbook.


Faculty Research Data
UC Berkeley Research Faculty and their research partners may publish and share datasets through UCB Library’s Dataverse. All datasets are reviewed by a curator prior to publication, who reviews datasets for quality control, metadata, and proper documentation.
Before using data in this collection, please review the license, any custom terms of use, and contact the dataset author or the Data + Digital Scholarship Services with questions. For more information please see UC Berkeley Library Dataverse FAQs.


Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) Polls
The Berkeley IGS Poll is a periodic survey of California public opinion on important matters of politics, public policy, and public issues. The poll, which is disseminated widely, seeks to provide a broad measure of contemporary public opinion, and to generate data for subsequent scholarly analysis. The poll was previously titled the “California Public Opinion Poll,” which is organized by decade and goes back to 1950.

title: About
text:
Data Not in Dataverse

GIS data
Most GIS data held by UC Berkeley Library can be found in our GeoData Portal, which holds data for areas around the world, with an emphasis on the nine county San Francisco Bay Area and northern California.
GIS data in UC Berkeley Library Dataverse is limited to faculty research data or licensed datasets accessible only to UC Berkeley affiliates.


Articles, Preprints, Dissertations, Conference Presentations and other documents
eScholarship is the University of California’s Institutional Repository for traditional scholarly outputs.

title: Can I publish code with the Faculty Research Data Collection?
text: While the Faculty Research Data Collection supports deposits of any file type, we recommend publishing primarily code-based datasets to Zenodo. Please contact librarydataservices@berkeley.edu with questions.

title: Who can deposit data in the Faculty Research Data Collection?
text:
UC Berkeley senate faculty, or a researcher designated by the faculty member to use their allocation, may deposit data for publication.
Funding for this data publishing service, which is a component of the Data Storage Allocation pilot program, was made available following advocacy by the Senate Committee on Information Technology (CIT) and DIVCO to address data storage issues faced specifically by faculty. As a result, the scope of this initial pilot is focused on senate faculty.

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Request Upload Access
Submit a deposit interest form with basic information about your dataset.
A member of Data + Digital Scholarship Services will review your request, grant you upload access, and follow up with next steps before you proceed.

title: Deposit Your Data
section: Log In and Create a Dataset
text:
Log In and Create a Dataset
Log in to UC Berkeley Library Dataverse with your CalNet ID and navigate to the Faculty Research Data Collection.
Click “+ Add Data” → “New Dataset.”
Select a dataset template that matches your subject area, or select “None.” Templates pre-populate certain fields but don’t limit what metadata you can enter.






Important



If you don’t see an “+ Add Data” button, your upload access may not yet be configured. Contact librarydataservices@berkeley.edu to adjust your permissions.

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Add Required Metadata
Fill out the following required fields:

Title — main title of the dataset
Author — people or organizations that created the dataset
Point of Contact — entity users can contact; email required
Description — summary of purpose, nature, and scope
Subject — area of study

Hover over the  icon next to any field for its definition.

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Upload Files
Drag and drop files into the upload area, or click “Select Files to Add.” To preserve folder structure, upload a .zip file. Maximum 1,000 files per batch — for larger deposits, see API upload instructions on GitHub.
Dataverse automatically creates archival .tab versions of Stata, SPSS, R, Excel, CSV, and TSV files. Your originals are preserved.
Click “Save Dataset.”






Tip



A DOI is reserved as soon as you save. You can include it in manuscripts or grant applications now — it will resolve publicly once the dataset is published.

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Add Supplementary Metadata
Return to the dataset page → Metadata tab → “Add + Edit Metadata”
Add all metadata relevant to your discipline. You don’t need to complete every section, only those that apply to your dataset.

Citation Metadata (all deposits)
Geospatial Metadata
Social Science and Humanities Metadata
Astronomy and Astrophysics Metadata
Life Sciences Metadata

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Set Terms and Access
Return to the dataset page → Terms tab → “Edit Terms Requirements” and select a license:

CC0 1.0
CC BY 4.0
Or select “Custom Terms” to define your own terms of use

Optionally, you may enable a guestbook to collect user information before download. Select “Standard Guestbook — Faculty Research Data.” Guestbooks are not generally recommended for open access datasets (e.g., CC0, CC BY 4.0).
For licensing guidance, contact Scholarly Communication and Information Policy: schol-comm@berkeley.edu

title: Deposit Your Data
text:
Submit for Review
Click “Submit for Review” on the dataset page, confirm your license, and submit.
Your dataset will be reviewed following the CURATE(D) model. A member of Data + Digital Scholarship services may suggest changes to improve reusability.






Warning



Once published, a dataset cannot be deleted — only new versions can be created. See Dataset Versions for details.

title: Prepare Your Data
text:
When preparing your dataset for publication, consider the following:

Completeness: UC Berkeley Library Dataverse is designed for finalized data.
Documentation: Include or create documentation (such as a README or codebook) that describes how your dataset was created, defines all variables, and identifies relationships between files. See the Cornell’s Writing READMEs for Research Data guide.
Preservation: Use open file formats where possible and closed formats only as necessary.
File Organization: Use consistent file and folder naming conventions.
